text:
jordan: Heads up — ACME tenant reported sudden p95 token-latency spikes (~1.6s -> 3.2s) on their dedicated pool starting ~14:23 UTC, also saw transient 429s. Can someone triage?
emma: saw the alert, digging into autoscale events. It looks like the pool did scale but didn't drain older pods correctly. attaching short logs.
ivan: FYI ACME is on fractional MIG config (2g.10gb slices) on H100v2 nodes. We saw similar odd bursts earlier but not this amplitude.
maya_sre: pinging the runtime traces — curious if SM saturation from a particular kernel is correlated. Do we have per-slice SM utilization?
jordan: attaching sample trace snippet and the customer repro steps (from their report):
```
# repro
1) send 6 concurrent chat/generate calls (seq len 512) to /v1/generate
2) token rate ~ 500/sec per client
3) after ~30s p95 jumps, requests get 429 for ~45s
```
emma: runtime logs (short):
```
2026-02-18T14:22:51Z pool-scale: add 2 pods
2026-02-18T14:23:05Z pod-42 sat 100% mem
2026-02-18T14:23:12Z node-5 slice-1 sm_util=98% kernel=attn_fwd_v2
2026-02-18T14:23:18Z router: 429 -> token bucket full
2026-02-18T14:24:05Z pod-41 evict backlog
```
ivan: that kernel name matches the custom fused-attn kernel we rolled last month. It tends to be efficient but can spike SM usage when batch sizes vary. Fractional slices have tighter SM headroom.
maya_sre: can we repro on repro cluster? I'll spin up a dedicated node with identical fractional config and run ACME's steps. If we can reproduce, we'll try disabling fused kernel (fallback to generic attn) to see change.
jordan: I already asked ACME for a short tenant config + example request body, they sent it. Pasting minimal payload: `{"model":"rwlm-13b-q2","max_tokens":1024,"input":"<chat>","batch":1}`
emma: quick check of autoscaler: policy fired at 14:22 to add pods, but cooldown was 60s and router still had backlog; autoscale didn't increase burst capacity. filing an infra follow-up.
ops-bot: [incident] ticket #INC-2429 created for tenant-acme: "p95 spike + 429s on fractional MIG slices"
ivan: repro attempt on repro-node (H100v2, 2g slice) — workload reproduced p95 spike in ~28s. Kernel attn_fwd_v2 SM time jumped and NVLink remained stable.
maya_sre: good repro. Next step I toggled kernel path (env OVERRIDE_KERNEL=generic_attn). re-run. p95 dropped from 3.2s -> 1.1s, no 429s observed. That strongly implicates fused kernel behavior under fractional slice.
emma: ops note: dedicated pool config currently uses aggressive fused kernels for perf. For fractional slices we may need a safety profile to prefer generic kernel when SM headroom < X.
jordan: customer wants mitigation ASAP — can we patch rollback to generic kernel for tenant-acme's pool as a short-term fix? They can't tolerate repeated 429s.
maya_sre: I can trigger a targeted config change for that pool to set KERNEL_PROFILE=conservative (won't touch model artifacts). Will schedule immediate rollout with canary 1 pod -> 3 pods, monitor.
ops-bot: deploy-bot: rollout start: config/kernel-profile -> conservative (pool: tenant-acme-dedicated) at 14:59 UTC
jordan: customer confirms they saw improvements after 30s, p95 back to baseline, thanks.
ivan: root cause hypothesis: fused-attn kernel has higher peak SM occupancy for certain input patterns; on fractional MIG slices this reduces headroom and pushes slice into sustained saturation, causing request queueing and router-level 429s when token buckets deplete.
emma: remediation plan: 1) urgent: apply conservative kernel profile to affected fractional pools (manual) 2) short-term: adjust autoscale burst thresholds for fractional pools 3) mid-term: runtime should select kernel variant based on per-slice SM headroom heuristic 4) long-term: add per-slice kernel telemetry and a safety circuit to fallback automatically.
maya_sre: opened follow-up RFC for heuristic + telemetry (RFC-873). I'll attach perf numbers from repro.
jordan: customer requested a note for billing: they saw no overage but were worried about retries — confirm no billing anomalies for the 45s window?
emma: checked billing logs — no double-charges; clients received 429s, so requests were rejected, not retried by server. I'll send a short customer message.
ivan: one-off note: fractional slices are more sensitive to kernel selection. Recommend we document this in the Dedicated best-practices doc and flag as known limitation for certain fused kernels.
maya_sre: monitoring follow-up: create alert if per-slice SM_util > 90% for >20s on fractional configs. I'll add alert and a dashboard tile.
jordan: thanks team. I'll update ACME with the mitigation steps and link to the ticket.
ops-bot: ticket INC-2429 updated: mitigation applied, monitoring added.
emma: closing loop — keep thread open for 24h to confirm stability. If no regressions, we'll transition to RFC and schedule kernel tuning.
jordan: noted, leaving thread open. :white_check_mark:
